text:
lena: Heads upI was walking a new user through the Python quickstart and hit multiple problems in the repo sample. Thought I'd surface here.
omar: Sorry about that 615 what did you find?
lena: Repo path: `docs/quickstarts/python/simple-chat/`. Problems: Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT points at `/usr/local/bin/python` but the image uses `python3` binary. Also the README instructs `pip install -e .` but the package name in setup.cfg is `redwood-inference` so the import examples show `import redwood` which errors.
tara: Oof import mismatch. So example code shows `from redwood import Client` which fails with ModuleNotFoundError.
mike: Is there also an async/sync mismatch? I've seen that before.
lena: Yes, the README has an `async def main():` example but then the snippet calls `client.generate_sync(...)` which doesn't exist. New users get confused about which API to call.
omar: Can you paste the exact failing snippet?
lena: Sure:```python
from redwood import Client

client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")

async def main():
    resp = client.generate_sync("Hello")
    print(resp.text)

main()
```
tara: Yikes. Multiple problems: wrong package name, wrong method name, and not awaiting async functions.
mike: Also worth adding a note about proxy environments. I hit an issue where `pip` inside the sample Dockerfile didn't pick up `HTTP_PROXY` so builds in corp envs fail. We should add `ARG http_proxy` and `ENV http_proxy=$http_proxy` to Dockerfile for reproducible builds.
lena: Link checker just pinged me: `link-checker-bot` says the quickstart README references `https://docs.redwood.ai/python/quickstart` which 404s. Probably moved to `/docs/sdk/python/quickstart`.
link-checker-bot: [automated] Link failure reported for `docs/quickstarts/python/simple-chat/README.md` at 1845678955.
omar: Action items: 1) fix package/import to `redwood_inference` or update setup.cfg to provide `redwood` top-level package, 2) replace `generate_sync` with correct sync wrapper or show `asyncio.run(main())`, 3) update Dockerfile for proxy args and shebangs, 4) correct docs links.
tara: I'll open a docs PR to change imports and update code blocks to both sync and async idioms. I'll also add a tiny test in CI that runs `python -c "import redwood_inference"` inside the sample image to catch import regressions.
mike: I'll add the Docker proxy bits + change ENTRYPOINT to `#!/usr/bin/env python3` in the container script and add a note about Alpine needing `py3-pip`/`python3` packages.
lena: Can we also add type hints in examples? Current snippets use `resp` but not typed. New users love typed examples: `from redwood_inference import Client, GenerateResponse` and `resp: GenerateResponse = await client.generate(...)`.
omar: Good call. Add `devex` and `docs` labels to the PR. main-only landing is fine.
tara: I'll include a small changelog line so support can point folks to the fix.
lena: Thanks all, please @mention me on the PR. I'll re-run link-checker and CI locally before merging.
